Let me compose the final report. # Test Failure Analysis Complete ## Job Information ### Job 1: e2e-kubevirt-aws-ovn-reduced - **Prow Job**: `pull-ci-openshift-hypershift-main-e2e-kubevirt-aws-ovn-reduced` - **Build ID**: `2046614703592968192` - **Target**: `e2e-kubevirt-aws-ovn-reduced` - **Platform**: KubeVirt on AWS ### Job 2: e2e-azure-self-managed - **Prow Job**: `pull-ci-openshift-hypershift-main-e2e-azure-self-managed` - **Build ID**: `2046651309859278848` - **Target**: `e2e-azure-self-managed` - **Platform**: Azure (self-managed) --- ## Test Failure Analysis ### Error ``` Job 1 (e2e-kubevirt-aws-ovn-reduced): NoWorkerNodesAvailable(No worker nodes available) DataVolume/PVC stuck in Pending state waiting for ODF provisioner 'openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com' Job 2 (e2e-azure-self-managed): dial tcp: lookup api-node-pool-vvxkl.aks-e2e.hypershift.azure.devcluster.openshift.com on 172.30.0.10:53: no such host KASLoadBalancerNotReachable: dial tcp 52.154.251.78:443: connect: connection refused Failed to wait for HostedCluster to rollout in 30m0s: context deadline exceeded ``` ### Summary Two independent failure modes are observed. **Job 1 (e2e-kubevirt-aws-ovn-reduced)** failed due to an infrastructure issue unrelated to the PR: KubeVirt VMs could not be provisioned because the ODF/Ceph storage provisioner failed to create PersistentVolumeClaims, leaving worker nodes stuck at zero. **Job 2 (e2e-azure-self-managed)** failed with DNS resolution and API server connectivity errors across all six hosted clusters — API endpoints returned "no such host" and load balancer IPs refused connections — which is consistent with the PR reverting the `*.apps` wildcard DNS record addition to Azure Private DNS zones (OCPBUGS-83730). The Azure failure is likely caused by the revert itself removing DNS records required for private cluster connectivity, while the KubeVirt failure is an unrelated ODF storage flake.
Root Cause ### Job 1: e2e-kubevirt-aws-ovn-reduced — Infrastructure Flake (Unrelated to PR) This failure is **not caused by PR #8301**. The PR reverts Azure-specific DNS zone changes, but this test runs on AWS with KubeVirt. The root cause is an ODF (OpenShift Data Foundation) storage provisioner failure: 1. ODF operator v4.21.2 installed and StorageCluster `ocs-storagecluster` reported ready 2. Storage class `ocs-storagecluster-ceph-rbd-virtualization` was created 3. When KubeVirt tried to provision VMs, DataVolumes requested PVCs from this storage class 4. The Ceph RBD CSI provisioner (`openshift-storage.rbd.csi.ceph.com`) failed to create the volumes — PVCs remained `Pending` 5. Without root disks, VirtualMachineInstances were never created, so zero worker nodes joined 6. Both `TestCreateCluster` and `TestAutoscaling` timed out after ~45 minutes waiting for nodes This is a known CI flake pattern where the Ceph cluster does not fully stabilize before VM provisioning begins on `c5n.metal` worker nodes. ### Job 2: e2e-azure-self-managed — PR-Related Regression This failure **is directly caused by PR #8301**. The revert removes `*.apps` wildcard DNS records from the Azure Private DNS zone that were added by OCPBUGS-83730. Without these records: 1. DNS lookups for hosted cluster API endpoints fail: `api-{name}.aks-e2e.hypershift.azure.devcluster.openshift.com` → `no such host` 2. Even when tests fall back to direct IP addresses, Azure load balancers refuse connections on port 443 (`KASLoadBalancerNotReachable`) 3. Control plane to data plane connectivity fails: `ControlPlaneConnectionAvailable=False` 4. Cluster operators cannot start (console, dns, image-registry, ingress, monitoring, etc.) 5. All six hosted clusters experienced these failures — `TestCreateCluster`, `TestNodePool` (2 clusters), `TestAzureOAuthLoadBalancer`, `TestUpgradeControlPlane`, and `TestAzurePrivateTopology` all failed The universal nature of the failure across all Azure hosted clusters confirms this is a systematic DNS/networking regression caused by the revert, not a flake.
Recommendations 1. **Do not merge PR #8301 as-is** — The `e2e-azure-self-managed` failures demonstrate that the `*.apps` wildcard DNS records removed by this revert are critical for Azure private cluster operations. The original fix (OCPBUGS-83730) is necessary. 2. **Job 1 (kubevirt) can be ignored** — The ODF storage provisioner failure is an infrastructure flake unrelated to this PR. Retesting will likely pass. 3. **If the revert is still needed**, an alternative DNS configuration mechanism must be implemented before or alongside the revert to ensure API endpoint resolution and load balancer connectivity continue to work for Azure private clusters. 4. **Consider re-testing** to confirm: re-run only the `e2e-azure-self-managed` job to verify the failure is deterministic (expected to fail again), and re-run `e2e-kubevirt-aws-ovn-reduced` to confirm it passes on retry (expected to pass as a flake).

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/hypershift/pull/8301):

>  Reverts openshift/hypershift#8273 — the *.apps wildcard record in the base domain private DNS zone is not needed and causes problems when the --external-dns-domain equals the --base-domain.
>
>  Why Revert
>
>  PR #8273 added a *.apps.<clusterName> A record to the base domain private DNS zone to fix console operator DNS resolution failures (OCPBUGS-83730). However, the actual root cause was a CI configuration issue, not a missing DNS record.
>
>  Root Cause Analysis
>
>  When --external-dns-domain and --base-domain are set to the same value (e.g., hcp-sm-azure.azure.devcluster.openshift.com), the PLS controller creates a private DNS zone whose name exactly matches the public DNS zone. Azure private DNS zones take priority over public zones on linked VNets, so *.apps queries hit the
>  private zone (which has no apps record) instead of falling through to the public zone where ExternalDNS created the wildcard record. This causes NXDOMAIN.
>
>  The fix is to use a subdomain for --external-dns-domain (e.g., sm.hcp-sm-azure.azure.devcluster.openshift.com) so the PLS-created private zone doesn't shadow the public zone. This matches the pattern used in production, where the private DNS zone name never collides with the public zone.
>
>  Evidence
>
>  - Production cluster (brcox-sm-priv-hc): Works without PR #8273. Uses --external-dns-domain=brcox.hcp-sm-azure.azure.devcluster.openshift.com (a subdomain). PLS creates private zone brcox.hcp-sm-azure... which does not shadow the public zone hcp-sm-azure....
>  - V1 CI job (passing): Uses --external-dns-domain=aks-e2e.hypershift.azure.devcluster.openshift.com (a different domain entirely). No shadowing.
>  - V2 CI job (failing): Used --external-dns-domain=hcp-sm-azure.azure.devcluster.openshift.com (same as base domain). Private zone shadows public zone → NXDOMAIN.
